More than 900 families in Nuevo Laredo’s colonia El Progreso are a step closer to legal certainty over their homes, after the municipal government readied over 900 deed files for processing, El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo reported.

The city, through the Instituto Municipal de Vivienda y Suelo Urbano (Imvisu), holds an agreement with the federal Instituto Nacional de Suelo Sustentable that gives families an economic subsidy to complete the deed process. The next step is the signing of a mandate agreement between the municipality and the federal government, which moves the process into its final stage before deeds are delivered, the paper reported.

The subsidy covers the full cost of the formal deed — normally between 12,000 and 14,000 pesos — leaving families to pay only 1,000 pesos in administrative and measurement fees.

So far this year, more than 130 deeds for lots have already been granted in colonias such as Las Torres, where about 500 lots still lack deeds, according to El Mañana.

Sources: El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo, “Procesarán 900 escrituras a familias en la colonia El Progreso gracias a subsidio,” by Martha Martínez, Oct. 23, 2026.

title: 900 Nuevo Laredo families in El Progreso on track to get property deeds through subsidy
